threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get confused by the bus routes and end up on the 38 when you meant to take the 55. Classic new arrival move.
Caught the night bus home last week and a guy was trying to sell a broken umbrella as a 'one-of-a-kind masterpiece.' No one bought it, but he didn’t stop his pitch.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw an old man feeding pigeons while vigorously arguing with a street artist about who painted the best mural—it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a Kebab shop next to an art gallery, where the scent of grilled meat mingles with fresh paint. Truly, Berlin's contrasts shine here.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they still call it the ‘BART Station’ and not the ‘Civic Center’ after all the closures. Someone from here feels the train’s pain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that made a hard stop, sending a guy’s sandwich flying. He just stared at it, blank, while we all tried not to laugh.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: You’ll see tourists in the parks all day but miss how locals sit at the same corner café, sipping a caña and catching up. It’s the real Gràcia vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still staring at the metro map like it’s a cryptic treasure map, trying to decipher where the next L1 stop is.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground.' Everyone knows it's a London thing, but you can't quite let go of that tourist vibe yet.
Last night on the 35, a guy in a suit was passionately singing Show Me Love. The bus driver just shook his head and smiled. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid sell homemade lemonade next to the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn station while the BVG strike had everyone in chaos. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the BVG strikes always seem to happen right before the weekend? It's like clockwork. Guess they know how to keep us on our toes!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a real local when they roll their eyes at a BART delay but still have a backup plan involving a bike and some burritos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy serenading the whole bus with a ukulele. Got off at 6th and Market, still humming the tune. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just a postcard. They miss the late-night chats over cheap wine in hidden squares, where locals laugh off the noise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by how they still read the menu like a tourist; locals order tapas without hesitation and chat with the waiter.
